newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Oct 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Italy's Loris Capirossi won yesterday's Australian motor cycle grand prix after Honda team-mates and bitter rivals Mick Doohan and Alex Criville crashed out of the race less than two kilometres from the finish. Leading the entire race, except for the firt three corners, Doohan missed out on a victory when Criville's front wheel rammed his rear wheel, sending the two riders tumbling. Page 25.

Sarah Fitzgerald, Michelle Martin, Liz Irving and Carol Owens have steered Australia to a third successive title at the world women's team squash championship with a 2-1 victory over the second-seeded England. The Australians were always favourites for te title, but England's Cassie Jackman showed another spurt of fine form defeating Martin 9-3, 4-9, 5-9, 9-7, 9-7. Page 26.

After forfeiting the lead and a sure win in an exhibition race in Los Angeles by taking the wrong turn, North Wollongong ironman Phil Clayton blitzed the field to win the opening round of the Uncle Tobys Super Series at Duranbah Beach on the Gold Coast yeterday. Page 26.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Although the Wallabies won their first rugby union tour match against Italy A 55-19, at the Santa Maria Goretti stadium on Saturday night, second-rower Garrick Morgan will return to Australia after fracturing his ankle in the opening seconds of the match.Page 27.

Making their debut at their new home ground of Belmore Oval in front of a crowd of almost 7,500, UTS Olympic beat the Canberra Cosmos 1-0 last night, leaving them alone at the top of the soccer table. Canberra spent much of the second half playing a man short after Peter Mazis was sent off for receiving a second yellow card. Page 27.

Playing for only six minutes in his first NBA game, Boomer and Sydney Kings point guard Shane Heal scored five points and grabbed two rebounds to help the Minnesota Timberwolves to a 104-88 victory over the Vancouver Grizzlies in a pre-season game. Heal's next pre-season match will be on Tuesday when the Timberwolves meet the Pistons in Detroit. Page 27.
THE AGE

With just a month until the first Test against the West Indies, Shane Warne could not get through a day's district cricket for St Kilda without leaving the field to ice his spinning finger, but the Victorian skipper will lead his team against Tasmania in unday's Mercantile Mutual match at Opus Oval. Page 2.

Trainer John Hawkes announced last night that after considering a number of jockeys, including Greg Hall, Brent Thomson, Simon Marshall and Grant Cooksley, Darren Gauci had been chosen to ride Octagonal in the Cox Plate at Moonee Valley next Saturday. Pag 3.

The Melbourne Tigers will enter their third National Basketball League grand final in four years after beating the Canberra Cannons 91-87 in the deciding third game of their semi-final series at Melbourne Park last night. The Tigers reached a four-point ead with only 2.8 seconds remaining after Canberra's Simon Dwight accidentally tipped in an Andrew Gaze free-throw. Page 7.
HERALD SUN

Australia's Mark Philippoussis will face Swede Magnus Larsson in his first final of the year after beating fellow Australian Mark Woodforde 6-2, 7-6 (7-5), 7-6 (9-7) in the semi-finals of the Toulouse tennis tournament yesterday. Page 76.

After finishing second to Australia's Stephen Hodge by only 13 seconds in the time trial, American Scott Moninger finished the VicHealth Herald Sun cycling tour at the Albert Park Grand prix circuit 34 seconds ahead of Hodge. Page 80.

Rival trainer Lee Freedman will present Gai Waterhouse with written evidence to support her case against a three-month suspension when she meets the Australian Jockey Club stewards today. Waterhouse and jockey Kevin Forrester were given the same penalty for failing to ensure Gossips had the best possible chance of winning the Shannon Quality on September 21. Page 84.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Victorian Emma Carney won her section of the International Triathlon Union World Cup in Sydney yesterday for the second year in a row, finishing more than two minutes ahead of world champion Jackie Gallagher. Queenslander Miles Stewart won the men's secton, posting his second World Cup win in eight days. Page 29.

According to Sydney Blues' catcher Gary White, the Blues have made a poor start to the Australian Baseball League's 1996-97 season because of the city's lack of professional standard facilities. Sydney lost Friday night's seven-inning double header againt the Melbourne Reds, 3-1 and 7-2. Page 33.

After South Africa cruised to a seven-wicket win over Australia at the weekend, the Australian cricketers will freshen up their batting line-up and take a more aggressive approach to today's day-night encounter with India at Bangalore. Page 39.
-- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
